correctness.rationale: The exact pair-distance identity \(d_H=2w-r-t\) forces supports to meet at most once and forbids repeated nonzero symbols in a coordinate. This bounds each coordinate degree by \(w\) and yields \(|C|\le n\). At equality every coordinate degree is \(w\), so supports form a symmetric \(n_w\) configuration and symbols form a proper Levi-graph \(w\)-edge-coloring. Conversely every symmetric \(n_w\) Levi graph is \(w\)-regular bipartite and hence \(w\)-edge-colorable by König; the induced words have composition \(\llbracket1^w\rrbracket\) and distances \(2w\) or \(2w-1\). The package verifier realizes both directions on \(PG(2,5)\). The \(n=34\) threshold then follows from the published \(k=6\) configuration spectrum.

originality.rationale: Direct statement-level comparison separates three ingredients: the 2010 coding paper leaves the all-distinct weight-six cases \(n=33,34\) unresolved; the 2007 configuration paper proves the exact \(n_6\) existence spectrum; the 2012 survey gives the symmetric-configuration/Levi-graph framework but does not state the constant-composition equality correspondence. The new step is the two-way equality classification, including the symbol-to-edge-coloring map and its converse via König edge coloring. Targeted semantic and web searches found no indexed statement implying that bridge or the resulting \(N_{\mathrm{ccc}}=34\) conclusion. Residual risk remains for terminology-shifted older design-coding literature.
residual_risks: An older design-coding paper may express the same equality correspondence under generalized packings, one-factorizations, or incidence-matrix terminology without using constant-composition language.

value.rationale: The bridge resolves the exact gap highlighted in the 2010 weight-at-most-six coding tables: it converts the two missing seven-ary all-distinct cases into a known configuration-spectrum question and yields \(N_{\mathrm{ccc}}(\llbracket1^6\rrbracket)=34\).
